name: Earth Sapta
summary: In the Valley of Trials, an initiate who loses the Earth Sapta can ask Canaga Earthcaller for another. The replacement gives the young shaman a chance to commune with the spirits of the land, along with a warning to guard sacred draughts carefully.

sections.title: A Second Chance with the Elements
sections.body: A misplaced Earth Sapta can interrupt an initiate's communion with the spirits of stone and soil. Prepared through specific rituals, the elemental brew thins the veil between the physical realm and the spirits. When an initiate loses or spills it while traveling through Durotar, Canaga Earthcaller prepares another in good faith, but warns the novice to guard sacred gifts with greater care.

sections.title: Canaga's Guidance
sections.body: Canaga Earthcaller watches over fledgling shamans emerging from the Den in the Valley of Trials. He understands that young orcs and trolls are prone to the chaos of early trials, but stresses that elemental spirits do not take kindly to negligence. Accepting a second sapta offers a small lesson in humility: power granted by the earth must be guarded and respected.

faq.answer: The Earth Sapta is a specially prepared ceremonial draught for shaman initiates. Drinking it grants spiritual sight, letting them perceive and speak with elemental earth spirits unseen by ordinary eyes.

faq.q: Why does Canaga Earthcaller offer this quest?
faq.answer: Canaga Earthcaller offers a replacement when an initiate loses or misplaces the Earth Sapta before completing the communion ritual during the Call of Earth trials. He provides another in good faith so the acolyte can finish their spiritual task.

faq.q: Where does this ritual take place?
faq.answer: The exchange takes place in the Valley of Trials, a sun-scorched canyon in southwestern Durotar where young orcs and trolls begin their journeys of discipline and honor.

faq.q: Is losing the sapta seen poorly by the spirits?
faq.answer: Canaga reminds initiates that treating sacred draughts carelessly shows a lack of focus. A true shaman must treat every elemental gift with absolute reverence.
Practicing shamans seeking to attune themselves to their first elemental totem, the Earth Totem, may prepare and drink the Earth Sapta.

faq.q: What happens after an initiate drinks the sapta?
aliases: what does sapta do when drunk
faq.answer: Drinking the draught opens an initiate's inner vision, allowing them to find and speak with a local manifestation of the earth spirit tucked away in the crags of the Valley of Trials.

angles.text: As an initiate shaman, losing the sapta teaches you discipline: communion with the elements requires steady focus and careful hands.
As an orc, you learn the ancient ways of shamanism in Durotar's arid crags, proving your dedication to the ancestors and the earth beneath your boots.
As a Darkspear troll, you learn to balance traditional loa worship with direct reverence for the elemental spirits in the Valley of Trials.
